title: Member selection with pointers and references
recap: The dot operator selects a member of an object or a reference to an object. The arrow operator selects a member through a pointer and corresponds to dereferencing then using dot.
Member selection through a null pointer is invalid. Establish pointer validity before accessing any of its members.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice member selection with pointers and references.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement incrementCounter(counter,delta). Return false for nullptr and do nothing. Otherwise add delta to the pointed-to Counter's value and return true. delta may be negative or zero and results fit int. Practice the -> operator for pointer member selection.
hints: Update counter->value, not a local copy.
A zero delta still counts as a successful operation.
